# Replication across populations

## What dogs see

![](media/dog-vision-compared-to-human-vision.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Illustration of dog color spectrum compared to human color spectrum."}

:::{.source}
Illustration by <a href="https://petsittingmalta.com/dog-vision-explained/">Pet Sitting Malta</a>
:::


## What do dogs prefer?

::: {.r-stack}
![](media/royetal2025_setup.jpg){fig-alt="Brown and white street dog approaching wooden tray with blue, yellow, and grey bowls."}

![](media/royetal2025_data.jpg){.fragment height=550 fig-alt="Dynamite plot of percentage of each color bowl (blue, grey, and yellow) as first choice. Twice as many dogs chose yellow compared to blue or grey."}
:::

::: {.source}
[Roy et al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10071-024-01928-9)
:::

## Replicate Roy et al. 2025

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Research Question

::: {style="font-size: 40px"}
Do pet dogs in the U.S. prefer the color yellow?
:::
:::

![](media/color_bowls_linus.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Brown and white dog sitting behind grey, yellow, and blue bowls."}


## Experiment 1 methods

![](media/bowls_color.jpg){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Brown and white dog sitting behind grey, yellow, and blue bowls."}

* Tested 75 dogs at dog parks, dog bars, etc.
* Chose between grey, yellow, and blue bowls
* Recorded first bowl approached

## No color preference

![](media/color1.png){fig-align="center"  fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects for each bowl color showing stronger preference for yellow over blue."}

## Experiment 2 methods

![](media/bowls_color.jpg){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Brown and white dog sitting behind grey, yellow, and blue bowls."}

* Tested 134 dogs under 7 years old at dog parks 
* Chose between grey, yellow, and blue bowls
* Recorded first bowl approached 
<!-- * Some trials with no food -->


## Dogs preferred yellow

![](media/color2.png){fig-align="center"  fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects for each bowl color showing stronger preference for yellow over blue."}

<!-- ![](media/color_yellow_linus2.png){.absolute top=120 left=550 height=500 fig-alt="Brown and white dog sitting with nose in yellow bowl."} -->


<!-- ## No effect of food present/absent -->

<!-- ![](media/color_food2.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects choosing blue, grey, and yellow bowls with separate panels for with and without food."} -->

## No effect of position

![](media/position.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects chooseing blue, grey, and yellow bowls with separate panels for purebred and mixed breed dogs."}


## No effect of sex

![](media/color_sex.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects choosing blue, grey, and yellow bowls with separate panels for males and females."}


## No effect of purebreed/mixed breed

![](media/color_breed.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects choosing blue, grey, and yellow bowls with separate panels for purebred and mixed breed dogs."}


## No effect of weather

![](media/color_weather.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects choosing blue, grey, and yellow bowls with separate panels for cloudy, rainy, and sunny weather."}



## But what else might cause preference?

![](media/royetal2025_setup_bowls_flipped.jpg){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Image of wooden tray with blue, yellow, and grey bowls."}

![](media/bowls_color_cropped.jpg){.absolute top=250 left=175 width=700 fig-alt="Image of wooden tray with blue, yellow, and grey bowls."}

![](media/bowls_color_filter_cropped.png){.absolute top=450 left=175 width=700 fig-alt="Image of wooden tray with blue, yellow, and grey bowls using a filter for dog vision."}


## Experiment 2 methods

![](media/bowls_grey.jpg){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Illustration of light, medium, and grey bowl."}

* 141 dogs under 7 at dog parks, bars, and daycares
* Chose between light, medium, and dark grey bowls


## Dogs didn't prefer light grey

![](media/color3.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects choosing light, medium, and dark grey bowls showing slight preference for dark bowls."}


## Summary

::::{.columns}
:::{.column}
:::{.incremental}
* We replicated Roy et al. (2025)

* Similar preferences across two (very different) populations of dogs

* Brightness can't account for this preference
:::
:::
:::{.column}
![Photo by <a href="https://unsplash.com/@moob?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText">Ayla Verschueren</a> on <a href="https://unsplash.com/photos/a-dog-playing-with-a-toy-on-the-floor-pd0DfUgaAf4">Unsplash</a>   
](media/dog_puzzle.jpg){fig-alt="Brown and white dog playing with yellow dog puzzle." width=350}
:::
::::

## Summary

::: {.incremental}
* Multiple levels of variation

* Striking demographic variation across research sites

* Inconsistent reporting of demographics

* Carefully consider sample when comparing studies
:::
